$comment: Every limit the product enforces, in ONE file (F27). The api reads it directly; web/src/limits.json is a verbatim copy made by web/scripts/gen-tokens.mjs, so the UI can never quote a number the server does not enforce. Source: docs/01-mvp-spec.html §03 'Limits at launch'.

story_window_d.$comment: How far back a ship's story and her track may reach (F16). 30 days for a visitor, 90 with an account; the server clamps, so a hand-written ?from= three years back comes back as thirty days and not as an error. `line` is the inline limit line the story prints under the timeline — one template, so the UI can never quote a window the server does not enforce. There is no auth until M6, so today everyone is `anon`.
story_window_d.line: Showing the last {days} days. An account opens 90.

download_window_d.$comment: The slice a download may cover (F17), shorter than the story's own window on purpose: reading 30 days is cheap, handing 30 days of points over as a file is not. Used by the export endpoint (M4 step 5).

port_wait_window_d.$comment: How far back /v1/ports/{locode} looks for finished anchorages when it says 'typical wait' (F19). A week: long enough that a quiet Sunday does not empty the sample, short enough that the number still describes the queue a ship joins today. Widen it and the figure stops being news.

map_vessel_age_s.$comment: Two numbers, and they have to differ. `silent_after` is when we stop believing a ship is still transmitting: past it she is drawn silent and counted by F7's 'Recently silent' chip. `max` is when she leaves the map entirely, because the refinery's hot hash keeps a field forever and without the cut the fleet is padded with ships that stopped reporting days ago. Setting both to 24 h made a ship go silent in the same instant she vanished, so the chip could never show anybody — F7 says 'brights <=24 h silents', which only means something if a silent ship is still on the water to brighten. So: silent at 24 h, gone at 48 h, and a full day in between where she is visible AND silent. M3's gap detector opens its event at `silent_after` for the same reason.
